#100349. Madrid 5-Day Itinerary: A Guide to Culture, Gastronomy, and Local Life

📅 06 May 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2464 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nomadicmatt ↗ Open Full Page

Madrid 5-Day Itinerary: A Guide to Culture, Gastronomy, and Local Life

📅 06 May 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2464 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city.
  • Like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow.
  • I’ve been a few times over the years and the city never ceases to amaze me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city. Though it’s somewhat sprawling, the city boasts stunning architecture, incredible food, and an energetic nightlife that stretches until dawn. Over 10 million people visit the city each year, and the minute you step out to explore, you’ll understand why Madrid is one of Europe’s top destinations.

Like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow. It’s a city for night owls, where dinner starts late and the parties even later. But if you can embrace the laid-back pace of life, the slow meals, and the late-night vibes, you’ll have a more authentic visit and uncover the true beating heart of the city’s culture.

I love all my visits to Madrid. I’ve been a few times over the years and the city never ceases to amaze me. The food, the energy, the art (so much art!). Madrid is just cool.

Sources indicate that being such a massive city, I know it can be easy to feel lost. Where do you start with what you want to do? Where do you go? It took me a few visits to figure it out.

In this post, I’ll help you plan an epic five-day visit to Madrid that will ensure you not only see the main sights but that you also get off the beaten path and see just what makes Madrid so popular — and all without breaking the bank either!

This first day focuses on a prestigious area designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021. There are over 40 monuments and over 40 buildings on the site. It’s easily one of the most picturesque and historic areas of the city.

The route begins at the Prado Museum, one of the best museums on the planet. Here you’ll find works from El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya, as well as many other masters (such as Rubens, Botticelli, and Caravaggio to name a few). If you only visit one museum in Madrid, this is the one. It’s incredible and worth taking the time to explore. It’s one of the biggest museums in the world, too. Make sure you spend a few hours here at a minimum.

Just a 10-minute walk along the Paseo del Prado, the journey continues at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, a private collection spanning from the Renaissance to Pop Art, and culminates at the Reina Sofía Museum. The Reina Sofía National Art Center offers a fantastic collection of modern art. Works by masters like Picasso, Miró, Kandinsky, Dalí, and Bacon can all be found here. The centerpiece is Picasso’s famous Guernica, a 1937 oil painting considered the most moving anti-war painting in the world. While I don’t love modern art, even I enjoyed this museum.

After museum hopping, it’s time to dive into Madrid’s culinary scene. Try Taberna La Fragua de Vulcano for a rustic atmosphere perfect for sampling cocido madrileño. If you are near the Reina Sofía Museum, don’t miss the vibrant garden terrace at Arzábal, renowned for having some of the best croquetas in the city. Finally, for a unique setting, Bodega de los Secretos lets you dine in restored 17th-century wine caves, making it the most atmospheric choice near the Prado Museum.

After a late lunch, spend some time exploring Madrid’s unique ‘House Museums. These are former private palaces that preserve the intimate atmosphere of their original owners. The crown jewel of this collection is the Sorolla Museum, the sun-drenched former residence of ‘the painter of light.’ Following a major architectural renovation, this underrated museum is set to reopen its doors in 2026, offering a refreshed look at its stunning gardens and Mediterranean canvases.

Or if you want something else, there is also the nearby Museum of Romanticism, where you can enjoy a coffee in its secret garden, or visit the Lázaro Galdiano Museum to marvel at a private collection of Goya, Murillo, Velázquez, El Greco, or Bosch housed in a magnificent neo-Renaissance mansion.

In the evening, enjoy some food and relaxation.

It has been revealed that the second day delves into the medieval and Renaissance layout of the city, famously known as Habsburg Madrid (Madrid de los Austrias). The central hub is Puerta del Sol, where a photo at Kilometer Zero and the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue are mandatory for a traveler’s geographic check-in. Kilometer Zero is the official starting point of all the highways and railways in the country, making this effectively the center of the entire country. There’s a small plaque you can snap a photo of.

Recent findings suggest that nearby is the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue (El Oso y el Madroño). The statue shows a bear reaching up to eat fruit from a madroño tree, symbols which come from Madrid’s coat of arms (the bear represents the city and the tree represents the land and nature surrounding it that has helped make it prosper).

It has been revealed that from here, walk toward the iconic Plaza Mayor, highlighting its porticoed architecture and the Casa de la Panadería. Plaza Mayor once hosted bullfights, markets, symphonies, tournaments, and even executions. Now it’s ringed with tourist shops, cafés, and restaurants. It’s a good place from which to indulge in some people-watching, offers some good (though overpriced) bars, and occasionally has concerts and events.

According to recent reports, for a true “Local Life” experience, stop for a calamari sandwich in the nearby alleys. Your taste buds will thank you.

After a relaxing lunch and some people watching, head to the Royal Palace of Madrid. The largest palace in Western Europe, the Baroque-style palace was built in the 18th century and is home to over 3,400 lavishly decorated rooms. It was originally built on a former 9th-century Muslim fort and today functions much like an art museum with numerous works, including pieces by Caravaggio, Juan de Flandes, and Francisco Goya. Though it’s the official residence of the royal family, they don’t actually live here anymore, and the palace is only used for official state functions. You can walk through the palace (both self-guided and guided tours are available), starting at the grand stairway, and wander through lavishly decorated staterooms. There’s also the Royal Armory, which houses a collection of medieval weapons and armor.

It has been revealed that to end the day, head to the Almudena Cathedral. Unlike many of the famous medieval churches in Europe, this one was constructed in the late 19th century. It was finally completed in 1993 and was consecrated by Pope John Paul II. While the exterior has a Neo-Classical design (to match the nearby palace), the cathedral also has a Neo-Romanesque crypt with over 400 columns that you can explore. Be sure to head up to the dome for stunning views out over the city.

It has been revealed that madrid is a paradise for foodies. It’s one of the reasons I keep coming back. While there are plenty of food tours to take in Madrid, I suggest heading off on your own to explore. Begin at the city’s iconic gastronomic markets. The glass-walled Mercado de San Miguel is a must for gourmet tapas near Plaza Mayor. It’s popular with the after-work crowd and is a place I usually visit a few times on my trips. Additionally, local favorites like Mercado de San Antón in Chueca and Mercado de Vallehermoso offer a deeper dive into regional flavors. Just make sure to bring an appetite.

If you do want to take a food tour, consider doing a food tour. This post has more of my suggestions.

It has been revealed that for dinner, head to Sobrino de Botín, officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest restaurant. It was actually a favorite of Ernest Hemingway during his time in Madrid. For a more casual vibe, go ‘tapas crawling’ through the historic streets of La Latina or Barrio de las Letras.

Recent findings suggest that as the sun sets, head to the Gran Vía to experience Madrid’s world-class rooftop culture. Venues like The Roof at Picalagartos or RIU, 360º sky bar offer signature cocktails and dinner with breathtaking 360-degree views of the skyline.

For those who don’t eat meat, Madrid has actually evolved into one of Europe’s best veg hubs, boasting a vibrant vegetarian and vegan scene in neighborhoods like Malasaña, where plant-based versions of traditional Spanish dishes are now a staple of the city’s diverse culinary identity.

Madrid is the only European capital where nature, science, and royal history converge in a UNESCO World Heritage oasis known as the ‘Paisaje de la Luz‘ (Landscape of Light). But this prestigious area, encompassing the iconic El Retiro Park and the Paseo del Prado, is just the beginning of Spain’s monumental legacy. For more UNESCO wonders, take a day trip out of the city.

One popular destination worth visiting is the Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, a sprawling imperial masterpiece recognized by UNESCO for its historical significance. El Escorial is located just one hour from the city by car and was commissioned by Philip II in the 16th century. It’s a massive palatial complex that includes a monastery, library, palace, basilica, and tomb for Spanish monarchs. Yet as massive as it is, it feels more austere than other palatial complexes, likely owing to its granite walls and symmetrical layout.

Another option for a day trip is the Royal Palace and Gardens of Aranjuez, a World Heritage Cultural Landscape that rivals the beauty of Versailles. Located just one hour south of the city, this was originally a hunting lodge, also commissioned in the 16th century by Philip II. It’s a blend of Renaissance and Baroque styles, with lavish rooms filled with tapestries, porcelain, and ornate decorations. There is lots of greenery and gardens here, which is partly why the royal family used this as their spring residence.

According to recent reports, lastly, there’s the historic university city of Alcalá de Henares, the birthplace of Spanish novelist, poet, and playwright Cervantes (he wrote Don Quixote). Just 45 minutes away by car, it also holds its own UNESCO World Heritage status, offering a perfectly preserved look into the Spanish Golden Age (1492–1659).

On your last day, it’s time to get further off the beaten path. Step back into the Golden Age at the Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales and the nearby Royal Monastery of La Encarnación, two hidden palaces that house breathtaking royal art collections behind their cloistered walls.

The Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales is a convent founded in 1559 by Joanna of Austria (sister of Philip II). The name “Descalzas Reales” (which means “Royal Barefoot Ladies”) refers to the Order of Saint Clare nuns who lived here in relative austerity. What makes this monastery unique is that many aristocratic women took refuge here, often bringing their artworks and other valuables. Over the years, this turned the convent into a veritable treasure trove of art.

Recent findings suggest that the Royal Monastery of La Encarnación was founded in 1611 by the wife of Philip III, Margaret of Austria. It was a royal convent, meaning it had the direct support of the monarchy. While the exterior has an austere Baroque style, the interior is quite lavish, with ornate chapels, colorful frescoes, and lots of religious sculptures and paintings. It’s also home to several notable relics, including a vial said to contain the blood of Saint Januarius. While tours are available, it’s still an active convent so parts are not open to the public (which, honestly, makes it all the more interesting to see).

To end your day with a local touch, head to the vast Casa de Campo park. This is the largest public park in the city, created in 1931. It covers a whopping 17 square kilometers (6.5 square miles) and includes an artificial lake, lots of paths, a zoo, and even an amusement park. Here, you can enjoy a scenic lunch or dinner at one of the lakeside terraces, offering an unrivaled view of the Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral across the skyline. It’s the perfect place to end your trip.

Sources indicate that while Barcelona tends to get more attention, I think Madrid is one of the best cities in Europe. It boasts a mouthwatering culinary scene, a raucous nightlife, and tons of things to see and do — no matter your interest or budget. I’ve been visiting the city for almost two decades and never get tired of the tapas, architecture, and history. The city just packs so much in and there really is something for everyone here. By following the itinerary above, you’ll see all the main sights while also getting off the beaten path in Spain’s historic capital.

QR codes are everywhere when we travel now, on restaurant tables, parking meters, hotel signs, airports, train stations, and transit machines. This travel scam known as Quishing or QR code phishing is becoming the fastest growing travel scam warning out there. Most QR codes are legitimate, but scammers are using fake QR code stickers and fake payment pages to catch travellers when they are tired, rushed, or distracted.

Industry observers note that QR code travel scam happens when a fake QR code sends travellers to a fraudulent website. The code may be placed over a real QR code on a parking meter, restaurant table, hotel notice, airport sign, or transit machine, or it may arrive by text or email pretending to be a fine, toll, ticket, or check-in request. A scammer does not always need to hack a system or damage a payment machine. Sometimes they print a fake QR code sticker and place it directly over a legitimate code.

You think you are paying for parking, ordering food, checking into a hotel, or settling a toll. Instead, criminals may be collecting your credit card number, password, phone number, licence plate, email address, or other personal information.

If it looks raised, crooked, bubbled, or mismatched, ask staff for a printed menu or the restaurant’s official website.

Parking is one of the easiest places for this scam to work because travellers are often rushed and confused.

Before paying through a parking QR code, inspect the sticker, read the URL preview, and check whether the payment page matches the city, parking authority, or official app named on the machine.

It has been revealed that if anything feels off, do not use the QR code. Type the official website yourself, use the official parking app, pay at the machine, or ask local staff for help.

In a recent development, airports and transit stations are full of QR codes: Wi-Fi, directions, tickets, luggage storage, forms, lounge access, and service information. Travel scams often happen when travelers are in a hurry. If you need wifi, a taxi, some food, QR codes are often the easiest way to catch you off guard.

Sources indicate that that does not mean every code is unsafe. It means you should slow down when a public QR code asks for payment, passwords, ID documents, or personal information.

The FBI warns that malicious QR codes can send people to fake sites, steal victim data, embed malware, or redirect payments. The FBI warns that criminals can tamper with QR codes to redirect payments, steal login and financial information, or send people to malicious websites.

The easiest way to avoid this scam is to build one habit before you scan a public QR code.

In a recent development, do not scan just because a sign looks official. Public signs, parking meters, table cards, and posters can be tampered with.

If the message says you must pay immediately, avoid a fine, settle a toll, confirm a booking, or prevent a penalty, slow down. Urgency is one of the biggest warning signs.

Before your phone opens anything, look at the QR code itself.

Now hiring: Staff to power Democrats’ probes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February.
  • Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the new year, making the most of their coming majority.
  • That means staffing up major committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February. He will be a key player in leading oversight efforts next year — and so will Democratic staff. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the new year, making the most of their coming majority.

That means staffing up major committees. And for the dozens of attorneys and other aides preparing to take on a belligerent Trump administration that has cast Democratic oversight as potentially criminal, the job will come with extra scrutiny.

In a recent development, arya Hariharan, former chief oversight counsel to Sen. Richard J. Durbin on the Senate Judiciary Committee and now a partner at Holland & Knight, said the pressure will be on from day one.

“Are you prepared to not sleep very much and know that every single thing you do is going to be scrutinized, every footnote, every comma?” Hariharan said.

Still, the way Hariharan sees it, serving on the Hill is worth it. “I hope they all fall in love with it because it’s a lovely place to work,” she indicates of staffers headed there for the first time.

According to recent reports, the work done by attorneys and other staff in oversight probes can rapidly become part of constitutional law. When Trump adviser Peter Navarro defied a subpoena from Democrats investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol, it touched off debates about executive privilege and contempt of Congress. Probes of Hunter Biden led to similar court fights.

Some questions have gone all the way up to the Supreme Court, like in Trump v. Mazars, when the House fought to access Trump’s business records during his first administration in furtherance of toughening up government ethics laws.

There’s every indication that pressure will continue in the fresh Congress. James Melendres, a partner at Snell & Wilmer, said Democrats are poised for aggressive oversight efforts, even if they know it could be tough to make headway against litigation resistant administration officials.

Sources indicate that “Democrats are going to have less than two years to show results. I think they are going to move really fast,” Melendres noted.

Democrats will likely soon start to send out preservation letters to private companies, institutions and others they intend to probe in the new year, if they haven’t already, Melendres said.

It has been revealed that “There may be significant pushback from the administration, from agencies and individual government officials who receive requests. I think third-party, nongovernment agencies and individuals are going to be high on the list for these committees,” he said.

In addition to the hiring that happens over the next few weeks, House Democrats will have major decisions to make about chamber and committee rules for the new Congress, including who will hold subpoena authority. And off-Hill observers will be watching closely.

“For companies, for individuals and their counsel, mapping all of that is going to be a massive part of the job between now and early January,” Melendres remarked.

Sources indicate that lawmakers need to nail down funding levels for congressional committees and staff — the amount of money involved can make a big difference in how big investigations get. Major committees, and major investigations, take a large amount of staff and expertise to get going.

For instance, the special House panel that investigated the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol spent about $14 million in less than 18 months, including for dozens of staffers.

Standing committees, such as Oversight and Judiciary, take a good chunk of change, too. In 2025 the House spent $12.9 million on the House Oversight and Government Reform panel, and $13.1 million on the House Judiciary Committee.

Those expenditures mean dozens of staff working long hours to review documents, send letters, send subpoenas and conduct interviews. Judiciary ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., who is expected to serve as chair next year, noted he wouldn’t get into specifics yet about how many resources the latest Congress may devote to oversight efforts.

“But we are talking about the most corrupt administration in the history of the United States, and this is an overwhelming and daunting task that faces us,” Raskin stated.

The Trump administration itself has already signaled it intends to push back forcefully on congressional oversight efforts.

Earlier this month, President Donald Trump described Democrats’ vows to investigate his administration as “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

Days later, the White House counsel sent a letter saying that subpoena threats from House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., and others “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.

According to recent reports, U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for the Southern District of Texas followed up with letters of his own to Sens. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.; and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., urging them to preserve documents tied to their promised oversight.

“The American people are entitled to freely associate without their elected officials terrorizing them with aggressive, harassing government action,” Reitz’s letter to Warren stated.

Members of the incoming majority have signaled they intend to defend themselves and their probes, and Blumenthal noted he won’t be deterred by the letter.

“There’s no way that I’m going to be intimidated or bullied. It would be laughable and ludicrous, but it is a clear abuse and misuse of prosecutorial powers and weaponization by the Department of Justice,” stated Blumenthal, who serves as the top Democrat on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

As for Raskin, he called the White House counsel letter and other missives “absurd on its face.”.

“I’m sure they would love to get into a whole series of letters and counter-letters and litigation. They’re trying to distract everybody from the fact that they just lost the worst landslide electoral repudiation in at least a half century in America, and so they’re going to pick a fight,” Raskin told reporters.

Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely incoming speaker, told reporters last week that he intended oversight efforts in his chamber to be led by Raskin and Garcia.

Sources indicate that “We haven’t ruled anything in. We haven’t ruled anything out. We’re going to follow the facts. We’re going to apply the law. We’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and we’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” Jeffries said.

Democrats have already publicly listed a handful of job postings for oversight staff and counsel, ranging from the Science to Armed Services to Judiciary panels, set to start early next year.

It has been revealed that beyond those hires, House Democrats will have to make one major pick they haven’t yet confirmed — the House counsel. The position, first created in the 1970s, is hired by the majority and advocates for the chamber in court. That attorney, along with a group of bipartisan House leaders controlled by the majority, will steer the chamber’s legal strategy.

In prior Democratic Congresses, that office has been active in court; Doug Letter frequently argued on behalf of the Democratic House majority seeking to enforce subpoenas on behalf of congressional committees. The position is held by Matthew Berry in the current Republican-controlled House.

“I mean, I think a lot of people are interested in that job,” Raskin stated.

  • As for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension strategy, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Türkiye is one of the world’s most visited countries, straddling the vibrant crossroads of Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. With sun-soaked Mediterranean beaches, Ottoman-influenced gastronomy, historic mosques, and bustling bazaars, it’s no surprise that the country attracted nearly 64 million visitors in 2025. But if your love of the country has you considering a prolonged vacation (or perhaps a second home), the government’s newly introduced golden visa might be a good fit—so long as you have $150,000 to spend.

Sources indicate that on November 17, Türkiye's president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed a decision to enact a upcoming foreign investor visa. The program offers two pathways: a $150,000 investment for a three-year residence permit, or $200,000 for a five-year stay (both of which can extend to the applicant’s spouse and dependents).

As for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension strategy, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds. No matter which pathway you select, you must hold your investment for at least half the visa term (as in, 1.5 years for the three-year visa or 2.5 years for the five-year visa). That means you could potentially withdraw your investment as early as after 18 months, according to IMI Daily, an investment migration trade publication.

The president’s announcement doesn't detail when or how foreigners can begin to apply, or the specific documents required. However, applications for the country’s other residence-by-investment permits require documents such as proof of financial means and health insurance, according to the government’s Investment and Finance Office.

If you don’t want to shell out $150,000, Türkiye offers other (renewable) relocation pathways. You may qualify for a two-year Short-Term Residence Permit for reasons such as tourism and university-sponsored research. Or, if your spouse is Turkish, you could apply for the three-year Family Residence Permit. Once you’ve lived in the country continuously for eight years, you’ll be eligible to apply for the indefinite Long-Term Residence Permit, which grants you almost all the same perks as citizenship, minus civic duties such as the ability to vote and mandatory military service.

Industry observers note that it's important to note that the new golden visa does not provide permanent citizenship. If you’re hoping to find your way into a passport, get ready to spend more. Türkiye’s citizenship-by-investment pipeline will require you to buy a home worth at least $400,000, invest at least $500,000 in sectors such as government bonds or venture capital funds, or, alternatively, help create at least 50 jobs.

Over the last few years, the influx of upcoming residency-by-investment programs has made it easier for wealthy travelers to relocate internationally. In New Zealand, you can invest $1 million New Zealand Dollars (about $567,300) in exchange for a three-year work-to-residency track. For Mediterranean living, Greece offers a five-year permit for a 250,000 euro (about $291,120) investment in a startup. Or, for a more affordable option, Paraguay has a permanent residency program for those who can invest $150,000 in “tourism projects” or $200,000 in stocks or real estate—putting it in line with Türkiye as one of the more affordable relocation options.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’re a digital nomad or a location-independent business owner, you’re either overpaying for fragmented insurance coverage (travel, medical, etc.) or just badly underinsured.
  • Sources indicate that the travel insurance organization Safety Wing is looking to change that.
  • I use their travel insurance all the time and they have just introduced what they call Nomad Citizen that seeks to address the gaps in coverage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re a digital nomad or a location-independent business owner, you’re either overpaying for fragmented insurance coverage (travel, medical, etc.) or just badly underinsured. You have a health strategy, travel insurance, and maybe some medical evacuation coverage. But, when you work for yourself, you lack the kind of safety net protections you get with a corporate job. And you cannot use a country’s social safety net because, well, you’re not a citizen, right? You’re just roaming the world!

Sources indicate that the travel insurance organization Safety Wing is looking to change that. They have always wanted to create this all-in-one package for digital nomads that includes insurance, employee benefits, and a social safety net.

I use their travel insurance all the time and they have just introduced what they call Nomad Citizen that seeks to address the gaps in coverage.

Industry observers note that nomad Citizen is an annual membership that bundles health coverage, travel protection, income protection, and life insurance benefits into a single plan. It’s for location-independent entrepreneurs and business owners who spend more than half the year outside their home country and whose lives and income cross borders as a default.

Nomad Citizen covers you globally with no residency restrictions (except for Puerto Rico).

In a recent development, but who should sign-up? This is an interesting product. I definitely think there’s a niche for it. After all, let’s say you’re an entrepreneur in Bali and don’t have access to any social safety net. What happens if you get sick or really hurt and you’re out of work? A friend of mine in Mexico was hit by a car and severely hospitalized and ate into his travel insurance limits really rapidly. Afterwards, he couldn’t work for months while he was in rehab and started a GoFundMe for help. A product like Nomadic Citizen would have helped him. Or helped any of the other digital nomads who get injured on the road and have to raise funds.

I think this product is good for someone who is living in a country outside their own without access to social services and a robust social safety net. For example, if you live in Sweden and have access to all the benefits of the State, this product probably isn’t for you because they have tons of services but if you live in Thailand, Mexico, Indonesia, or France but don’t have access to benefits, or are just roaming the world, have a high income, work on your own, or have a family, then this product would be something to consider.

Industry observers note that for those signing up on or after July 1, 2026, the Nomad Citizen membership costs $443 per month for those 18 to 39. If you’re 40 – 49, it’s $665 per month, and $875 per month for 50-55. Children cost $143 per month (couples on the plan can add their first child under 10 at no cost). You can pay monthly or annually.

A note about US coverage: Nomad Citizen is truly worldwide, including the US, although it should be noted that coverage limits were not designed for extensive use there…because well, the US health care system is just a mess.

It has been revealed that income protection: The income protection benefit is probably the single most compelling reason Nomad Citizen exists. Traditional income protection or disability insurance requires a fixed employer, a permanent address, and residency in a specific country. Freelancers and sole traders working across borders are essentially uninsurable for income loss through conventional schemes, such as government assistance.

If you’re a freelancer or remote worker and you lose your income (you’re laid off, your contracts dry up, or you can’t work due to a medical condition), Nomad Citizen pays you up to $4,000 per month for up to 3 or 6 months while you get back on your feet. That benefit doesn’t exist anywhere else!

Health insurance: Up to $1.5 million in annual coverage for inpatient, outpatient, prescriptions, dental, vision, mental health, maternity, preventive care, wellness therapies, and more. This is just like health insurance where you live and covers everything you need. It is far more robust than regular travel insurance, which is only there for emergencies.

Travel coverage: Trip delays, cancellations, stolen electronics, lost luggage, evacuation, robbery, family visits during hospitalisation.

Parental leave: If you have a baby or become a legal guardian of a child, they pay US$4,000/month so you can take time off work without worrying about money. There is a waiting period of 3 years to access this benefit.

Long-term disability: If something really serious happens to you and you are permanently forced to stop working because, for instance,  you lose your eyesight, you’re diagnosed with cancer, you have a major stroke, or you can no longer do basic things like walk, dress yourself, or eat on your own, they pay you US$4,000/month up to age 75.

Visa assistance: Members can browse and apply for different governments’ versions of long-term visas designed for nomads (i.e. they can work on those visas) directly through our app interface without having to apply through the government websites. They handle all the direct communication with the government and quality check your application before submission to maximize the chances of approval.

Nomad Care Map: Find the best providers through their member-powered database of more than 4000 healthcare providers all over the world, with ratings for service and English level.

It has been revealed that payment cards: Use your SafetyWing card to pay for covered services up to $500. This auto-generates a claim that has already been paid so you do not have to wait for reimbursement. The SafetyWing card is a worldwide prepaid debit card that is sent to every Nomad Citizen member, which they can use to pay for doctor’s appointments or prescriptions without using their own money.

24/7 human support: You’ll have access to 24/7 live chat so you can get an answer from a real person within a few minutes.

Everything in one app: Claims, coverage details, customer care, provider search with Nomad Care Map, and visa assistance are all managed through a single app. There is no need to switch between a health insurer, a travel insurer, and a separate income protection provider (if one existed).

For health coverage, you either pay out of pocket and file for reimbursement or contact the 24/7 team to arrange direct payment with the provider. For travel claims, you collect documentation (police reports, carrier delay notices, receipts) and submit a claim. For income protection, you work with SafetyWing to verify the loss and provide evidence that you’re actively seeking fresh income. Everything is managed through one app and they make it really simple and easy to do.

I love SafetyWing’s mission and use their travel insurance on all my trips. This new Nomad Citizen product is perfect for people who are full-time digital nomads and want some sort of income protection as well as more robust health and travel coverage and the kind of social safety programs you would get if you lived in one place. After all, when you are a solopreneur, you do worry about what happens if you get injured, can’t work, or have a kid. It’s all on you, right? Nomad Citizen is the program that ensures that you won’t have to worry about this kind of stuff anymore.

Latino Democrats celebrate midterm gains, with warning for party

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (685 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC.
  • Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.
  • Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.

But California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.

“Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” said Sánchez, who leads the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

Failure to address rising costs and push back against President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda could once again scramble the political calculus and spark another realignment in two years, said House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California.

“While Latinos shifted towards Democrats and … gave us this mandate as a party, Democrats must continue to earn their trust, not just every two years, but every single day,’’ he remarked.

Leaders of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus joined newly elected Latino members on Tuesday for a news conference to celebrate the recent wins and the role the group played in securing the House majority for Democrats. The caucus will boast 55 members in the next Congress, its largest roster ever, according to Sánchez.

BOLD PAC, the caucus’ campaign arm, invested heavily in Latino candidates this year, including in primaries.

California Rep. Salud Carbajal noted that BOLD PAC raised more than $18.5 million this cycle, which helped candidates leverage outside money.

Working-class majority-Latino districts in South Texas, Arizona and California were among the areas that provided Democrats with their biggest wins. Democrats capitalized on voter dissatisfaction over rising costs, the very issue that helped Trump and the GOP make significant gains among Hispanic voters just two years earlier.

But the wins weren’t limited to districts with sizable Latino populations.

Rep.-elect Denise Powell, who flipped a swing seat in Nebraska, credited BOLD PAC for playing a key role in her win.

“Yes, there are Latinos in Omaha, and those Latinos actually helped decide this race,’’ she stated. “BOLD believed in me as a candidate, but they also believed in our community.”.

Rep.-elect Bobby Pulido, who came to politics after a successful career as a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano singer, flipped a redrawn South Texas border district that Trump would have carried by 18 points in 2024.

“A lot of people feel like they don't belong to either party. But there's one thing about Latinos is we belong to each other,’’ Pulido said. “It's very hard to be a Latino right now in this country. … I expect to see us united, more united than ever, because it's a tough time right now.”.

Several of the winning candidates deployed novel strategies to reach voters. Pulido famously began performing at quinceañeras after his Republican opponent dismissed him as a performer.

According to recent reports, colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, who flipped a battleground district north of Denver, attended World Cup and Broncos watch parties. “If people don't hear our message, then it doesn't matter,’’ he said.

The candidates “met those voters where they were,’’ Sánchez stated. “They went into those communities and interacted in a very real and meaningful way. That's something I think that strategists or consultants don't always get. It's not just about pumping out lots of television commercials.”.

Recent findings suggest that amid those successes for Latino Democrats, Florida, home to one of the largest Latino electorates in the country, was a different story. Republicans held all three majority-Latino districts in the Sunshine State, though former news anchor Eliott Rodriguez, the son of Cuban immigrants, came within half a percentage point of unseating GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar in a district that backed Trump by 15 points in 2024.

Sources indicate that BOLD PAC did have a victory to celebrate in Florida, with Rep. Darren Soto, the deputy chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, narrowly prevailing in a district that Republicans redrew as one that no longer had a Latino majority.

“The redistricting wars ended up failing because of the investment by BOLD PAC,’’ Soto noted.

Sources indicate that there are a lot of eSIM companies in the world. They all work a similar way: you download their app, pick your package, install the eSIM into your smartphone, and off you go. There’s many I like.

But one I like more than the rest is Holafly and I’ve been using their eSIMs for years. I find their app to be easy to use and their rates really competitive.

Industry observers note that so when Holafly released Holafly Prepares, a single eSIM that works as an ongoing subscription across 160+ destinations, I was excited. It’s a great option for those who are looking for more data and flexibility than a traditional eSIM. (An eSIM is a digital SIM built directly into your phone’s hardware, so there’s no physical card to insert or swap. Instead of visiting a shop for a plastic SIM, you activate a plan by scanning a QR code or installing it through an app, and you’re connected within minutes. Because it’s software-based, a single phone can hold multiple eSIMs, letting you switch between a home number and a local or global travel plan without touching your device. I have like 10 installed. lol).

In this post, I’m going to explain what the product is, how it’s different than a traditional eSIM, and who I think this option is for!

You don’t reswap SIMs, you don’t redownload anything, there’s no re-purchasing, and no hunting for a new QR code every time you land somewhere new.

Recent findings suggest that it automatically reconnects you when you land in a latest place. Think of it as like a traditional mobile carrier – but a lot cheaper.

Industry observers note that you can buy it monthly or annually and it comes in two tiers: Light and Unlimited. There’s no annual contract and you can cancel any time.

The Unlimited Initiative includes no data caps and an unlimited hotspot so you can tether your laptop on the go. This tier also comes with a local phone number from the US, UK, or Canada, which lets you receive SMS messages.

The Light Proposal gives you 25GB of data a month, still includes a hotspot, and still covers the same 160+ destination coverage. For someone who mostly uses maps, messaging apps, and the occasional Instagram scroll, this package is probably the best option.

Additionally, with both Holafly Plans, once your plan is active, you get their “Always On” feature which is 1GB of backup data every month, automatically for life, even if you eventually cancel your subscription entirely.

Pricing varies a bit by region and currency and depending on how long you purchase, so check out their current rates on the Holafly Plans page. However, as an example, their unlimited blueprint is only $55 USD per month for 1 year, which is a lot cheaper than any US based carrier charges for their base option that includes unlimited 5G data overseas. You can get monthly, quarterly, or yearly plans. Quarterly plans save approximately 10% while yearly plans save 15%.

Use the promo code NOMADICMATT at checkout to get 10% OFF Holafly Intends and 5% OFF all standard Holafly eSIMs.

Classic Holafly eSIMs are built for a single trip. You pick a country or region (there are 200+ available), choose how many days of data you need, and it covers just that trip. If you’re flying to Portugal for two weeks, a classic eSIM is still the simpler, cheaper option. It’s a one-and-done purchase. If you only take a couple trips per year then this is still the best option.

On the other hand, if you’re a digital nomad who is gone from your home country most of the year and moving between different countries all the time, then the Holafly Looks fly is the much better option. It’s a standing global subscription designed for people who are more or less always somewhere. Instead of buying a newly introduced eSIM every time your itinerary changes, you have one number, one connection, one bill that follows you across borders indefinitely. Plus, you can get a phone number, unlimited data, and a hotspot. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if there's one thing better than having a vacation on the calendar, it's knowing you didn’t pay full price for it.
  • The annual event, which falls on the Tuesday after Thanksgiving—this year, on December 1—has become a prime moment for savvy travelers to score booking discounts, whether that’s a Caribbean beach escape in the depths of winter, a European summer adventure, or simply a long weekend somewhere newly introduced.
  • You don't have to wait until the official Travel Tuesday date to start saving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if there's one thing better than having a vacation on the calendar, it's knowing you didn’t pay full price for it. And right on cue, one of the most exciting stretches of the travel-booking year is kicking off. With Thanksgiving around the corner, Travel Tuesday is already making its presence known, bringing early-bird deals on flights, hotels, cruises, and vacation packages for travelers ready to trade their wish lists for boarding passes.

The annual event, which falls on the Tuesday after Thanksgiving—this year, on December 1—has become a prime moment for savvy travelers to score booking discounts, whether that’s a Caribbean beach escape in the depths of winter, a European summer adventure, or simply a long weekend somewhere newly introduced.

The best part? You don't have to wait until the official Travel Tuesday date to start saving. Airlines and hotel groups are getting a head start with early promotions, and some of the most appealing offers—from top-rated cruise lines to flight fares—are already live. I've rounded up nine of the best early Travel Tuesday deals worth booking, or at the very least keeping an eye on as more are confirmed.

World of Hyatt has already dropped its annual Cyber Sale, slashing rates by up to 25% for its members across more than 1,250 hotels and luxury resorts across the globe. With a travel window stretching all the way through April 30, 2027, you have plenty of runway to lock in trips from a sun-drenched winter escape to a spring break getaway—or that bucket-list vacation you’ve been putting off. If you’re not a member yet, the sale is open to the general public for up to 20% off. (That stated, signing up takes two seconds and is totally free, so don’t leave the money on the table!) Just make sure to lock in your dates by December 8, 2026.

Save on Sandals Saint Vincent and The Grenadines—the perfect sanctuary for relaxation within over 50 acres of breathtaking Jurassic Park–like scenery.

Want the best bang for your buck in the Caribbean? Sister brands Sandals and Beaches have you covered. The early Travel Tuesday deals from these all-inclusives ensure up to $750 in air credits to help offset flight costs, alongside up to 65% off hotels and resorts across the entire resort portfolio—from Grenada to St. Lucia, Saint Vincent and The Grenadines, Curaçao, and beyond.

It has been revealed that select bookings promise some exclusive perks too: At Sandals Resorts specifically, travelers can receive up to $2,250 on booking and spa credits to use during their adults-only stay. Families booking Beaches Turks and Caicos (including the upcoming Treasure Beach Village) or Beaches Negril in Jamaica can receive up to $1,650 in booking and spa credits. Just book by Travel Tuesday itself for qualifying travel through December 31, 2028.

Whether you’re an avid traveler or not, there’s a high chance you’ve booked a flight, hotel, or rental on Expedia. Lucky for you, now just so happens to be the site’s biggest sale of the year, with savings on family beach resorts, romantic getaways, cabin retreats, and everywhere in between. If you’ve already got a special destination in mind, simply enter your city of choice and travel dates into the website or app’s search bar, use filters to refine your search, and see which Travel Tuesday deals come rolling in. Up until December 3, those ready to book via Expedia can save up to 50% on stays in cities all over the world—plus, onboard perks on select cruises, eligible discounts on car rentals, and more.

Industry observers note that in true holiday spirit, the ever-luxe and tropical hotel group Sun Siyam is offering up to 50% in savings across its six stunning resorts, from secluded barefoot hideaways in the Maldives to lush, high-end retreats in Sri Lanka. The timely sale allows for bookings made before November 30, and for eligible stays through October 31, 2027, depending on the property. Need more incentive to stay at Sun Siyam other than a discount at its fabulous locations? Easy—these stays come with memorable perks, like complimentary seaplane transfers, spa treatments, floating breakfasts, excursions, water sports, and dining experiences galore.

At Siyam World, for one, guests can save up to 50% while enjoying an all-inclusive meal plan. Meanwhile, at Sun Siyam Olhuveli, guests can receive 50% off airport transfers, 30% off à la carte dining, 25% off spa treatments, and 20% off water sports, with complimentary sunset cruises on qualifying stays. And there’s way more where that came from.

It has been revealed that it’s not often we find a “someday” trip at such a tempting price—but an early Travel Tuesday deal from Quark Expeditions puts that dream getaway well within reach. For those dreaming of the ends of the Earth, the cruise line is offering savings of up to 40% on select Arctic and Antarctic voyages. Available to book now through December 3, the limited-time promotion brings the world’s most exclusive polar frontiers within closer reach—from the icy wilderness of the Antarctic Peninsula and Svalbard to the rugged landscapes of Patagonia, Greenland, Iceland, and beyond. And yes, bucket-list itineraries—including the time-saving Antarctic Express: Fly the Drake—are also part of the offer.

Celebrity is launching this stunning river ship in summer 2027—and you can sail it for the best booking value yet.

Looking for a value-forward river cruise in picture-perfect corners of Europe? Top-rated cruise line Celebrity Cruises is releasing a set of flash sales over the next week, with its latest being a discount on exactly that—and the perks are pretty enticing. For one, if you book before November 24, you can save 75% on a second guest’s fare on sweet river sailings, from the Danube River to see Vienna and Budapest or venturing from Brussels to Amsterdam on a hunt for tulips. There are also select sailings—including a New Year’s cruise on the Rhine River—where you can save up to $1,000 in air credit per person.

When it comes to savvy ways to fly, it’s no secret that Skyscanner provides heaps of flight options and routes where value is front and center. If you’re looking to score cheap Travel Tuesday flights, you can count on the site for price drops on airfare over the next week through Cyber Monday. Along with vacation packages, hotel deals (at up to 35% off), and an app for price tracking, the Skyscanner website has an entire guide on and around Travel Tuesday itself—from advice on reducing fees to using shared loyalty points and beyond.

Whether you are mapping out a holiday road trip or chasing winter sun, scoring the right car rental deal is half the adventure. While highly regarded car rental manufacturer Avis has not yet rolled out an official Travel Tuesday promotion ahead of the December 1 event, you won’t have to wait to lock in some stellar savings. Right now, you can trim up to 35% off base rates simply by choosing the Pay Now option online, or unlock up to 30% off with Avis’s current discount code AWD S169100.

Book a discounted tour to the cloud forests of Costa Rica.

If you’ve got a sudden urge to get up and go, this is G Adventures’s biggest sale of the year—and it includes hundreds of early Travel Tuesday deals with up to 30% off tours and experiences across the globe. With some trips departing in the next 60 days, we’re talking discounts on some of the group’s most-loved and top-rated trips, including Thailand Island Hopping on the West Coast and chasing Costa Rica: Coastlines and Clouds Forests. If your schedule’s flexible and your passport’s ready, this is the kind of spontaneous deal you jump on before it disappears.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At first, the big hotel chains of the world laughed off Airbnb and vacation rentals. No seriously, they did. Now, they all compete in the vacation rental business and act like it was always the plan.

The problem for the traveler, is that almost all of the newer entrants just plug into a massive pipeline of already existing vacation homes and apartments and pop them on their own branded website with no added luxury, differentiation, amenity or expertise in curation.

It has been revealed that there’s no huge unlock of upcoming places or highly curated places that you could virtually always stamp as worth recommending to a friend, the way you’d rate an Aman, St. Regis, or Four Seasons hotel.

It has been revealed that this is precisely where Wander.com comes in, and it’s by far my favorite luxe vacation rental platform to date. The fact that it’s boutique and limited is what makes it, at least for me. And, the $350 off Wander promo code doesn’t hurt either.

Wander is a vacation rental company which truly hand picks every property that it lists, and has the exclusive listing on. Crucially, each of the vacation properties undergoes a sort of ‘Wander’ transformation to conform with brand standards for wifi, amenity, style and vibe.

It’s above my pay-grade as a blogger on this topic, but it seems like Wander co-invests in the real estate portfolio’s, or partners with owners in a unique way that’s far more integrated than others.

Where are they? Most Wander.com properties are scattered across the US, from the shores of Malibu to the great National Parks in Wyoming and all along the Eastern seaboard too. Hawaii is also a recent addition. Newly introduced destinations keep popping up!

Each of their properties feels uniquely wonderful and aspirational, and I’d say all have a very modern and contemporary slant to luxury. Grandma’s cabinets are not in any of these homes, but Tesla chargers are. One nice touch: each Wander offers a dedicated workspace with desk, chair, monitors and lightning fast wifi.

I completely respect that all tastes are individual, but the interiors and setups of these homes much more reflect my personal tastes, more minimalist chic, than many less curated vacation rental options.

Recent findings suggest that most Wander properties are around $1000 a night. Some will be half that, some will be double. On its face, that’s intimidating to many, but when you factor in the number of bedrooms and features it’s really reasonable. Families, or multi-family get togethers… amazing.

In a recent development, all Wander.com properties are at least two bedrooms and many are four, five or even twelve. One is an entire island with multiple residential complexes. For me, I love these sort of getaways for catching up with family or friends, and I never mind when other people are contributing too.

In a recent development, we’ve had some of our best ever vacations renting a house in Palm Springs for weeks or months at a time. Often, family or friends want in too, so we split the house and end up with two bedrooms each for under $500 per night.

That’s highly competitive in any hotel market for two rooms and the x-factor comes in the form of privacy, full on kitchens, gym facilities, often and a pool or entertainment area and laundry too.

In a recent development, we’ve used these bonus rooms and features to socialize or catch up with people in the serenity of the home, not annoyed by service, crowded pools or tight room setups. For a longer stay, I absolutely hate having to rely on a hotel kitchen for every meal. I love to hit a local market and grill with family or guests.

Recent findings suggest that wander is offering $350 off first bookings, which is a great way to get started. To browse the homes, you simply download the Wander app and start doom scrolling. When you find one you’re ready to book, the process is very self explanatory and easy to share with others.

I’m personally a fan of virtually California vacation and the properties offered on the platform cover everything from Palm Springs to Napa and all in between in stunning form. The $350 off is a solid discount and combined with new property discounts, which are frequent, there is a lot to love. You can browse Wander and download the app here.

If you don’t see the Wander.com discount in your account, you can add promo code AKFVDFD7 once the app is downloaded.

#100338. Where Was 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Filmed? Behind the Scenes in Spain and Germany

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (930 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

Where Was 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Filmed? Behind the Scenes in Spain and Germany

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television reveals, and more.
  • According to recent reports, we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens.
  • Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television reveals, and more. This time, we take a look at The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

According to recent reports, we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the action of the first film and tells the origin story of Katniss Everdeen’s grumpy tutor, Haymitch Abernathy, as he enters the Games himself.

Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.

Based on the books by Suzanne Collins, the dystopian series is set in a futuristic America in which each district must send a teenage tribute to fight to the death in an annual competition—the idea being that, by doing so, the public will be too afraid to rebel against President Snow.

This edition of the games is known as the Quarter Quell, with double the number of tributes being sent into the arena, meaning the stakes are so much higher. Interest in the film is high, not least because Haymitch is so beloved in the original series, portrayed by Woody Harrelson. Newcomer Joseph Zada takes the lead role in the latest film, while Hollywood heavyweights Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, and Kieran Culkin also star.

Industry observers note that one of the most crucial sets in the film is the arena where the games take place, and for this, director Francis Lawrence opted not for CGI and a green screen, but instead a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in northern Spain. Below, we look into the locations used in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Ben Wang as Wyatt Callow, Percy Daggs IV as Ampert Latier, Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Recent findings suggest that within the book and film series, the settings for the Hunger Games are always known to be virtually spectacular. For this film, filmmakers settled on the vast and untouched landscape of Somiedo Natural Park in the Asturias region of northern Spain, which boasts mountain ranges, glacial valleys, beautiful meadows, dense forests, and tranquil lakes. The remote region is also home to the last brown bear population in Europe.

When the tributes are rolled out into the arena, they are presented with a vast Cornucopia, a pile of weapons, food, and other supplies that might be useful to them in the competition. These scenes were filmed at Somiedo Natural Park, with the Asturian mountains and a glacial lake in the background.

It has been revealed that “Somiedo is a spectacular place,” said Pedro Aráez, supervising location manager. “The valleys, forests, and mountains have a very wild, untouched feeling, which was exactly what the filmmakers were looking for. It’s remote, dramatic, and visually unique. When you arrive there, you immediately understand why it was chosen.”.

It has been revealed that located close to Somiedo, the Teverga beech forest, Hayedo de Montegrande, was used for some of the dense woodland scenes, in which contestants battle it out and hide in the woods. Other scenes filmed here utilized a series of glacial lakes, the Saliencia Lakes and the Lago de la Cueva.

Iris Apatow as Proserpina Trinket and Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Before the tributes are introduced into the arena, they are first held in special little pods underground which are arranged in a circle around the Cornucopia. The perfect location for this? A velodrome, of course, which is steeply circular so cyclists can race around it. The film crew utilized Berlin’s Velodrom for this very purpose, with its cold, clinical silver decor perfect for matching the hi-tech aesthetic associated with the Capitol.

Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.

Prior to entering the Games, tributes must introduce themselves on the public stage, during a televised grand chariot parade in the Capitol. Another Berlin location with links to the sporting world was used for this purpose: the Olympiastadion. For fans of the earlier films, this is the moment when Jennifer Lawrence’s character Katniss becomes “the girl on fire” with her incredible flaming dress.

According to recent reports, the futuristic architecture of Edificio Calatrava in Oviedo, Spain—with its striking, claw-like structure—stands in for a building in the Capitol, where President Snow and his government live. The complex was designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, whose work is known for resembling living organisms. Meanwhile, the 14th-century Ehreshoven Castle, just outside of Cologne, was also used as a filming location, with local press reporting that its lush interiors might have been used to stand in for somewhere inside the Capitol.

A former smelting factory complex in western Germany, Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord provides the backdrop for one of the most atmospheric settings in the films, Haymitch’s home of District 12. The vast complex is able to stand in for multiple places within the district, a former mining town that has fallen on seriously bad times. Rather than being a desolate area stumbled upon by the filmmakers, Landschaftspark is popular for its nightly light installation by British artist Jonathan Park. There are also regular al fresco events here, from film screenings to the annual art-meets-sport Ruhr Games and Traumzeit Festival. Another location in Germany, Lindlar Quarry, was used for District 12, with wooden huts built here to resemble the outskirts of the village.

    #100334. Industry News: My First “New” Chase Sapphire Reserve Travel Redemption Blew My Mind

    📅 01 Jul 2025 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (877 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Godsavethepoints ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: My First “New” Chase Sapphire Reserve Travel Redemption Blew My Mind

    📅 01 Jul 2025 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Godsavethepoints

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, there’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card.
    • Recent findings suggest that the changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards.
    • Recent findings suggest that well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, there’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card. As per usual these days, the hot takes are plentiful and people are fired up. It’s either the apocalypse or the beginning of something great, depending on which attention seeker you read. As a long time cardholder, I’m really intrigued by the new changes.

    Recent findings suggest that the changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards. I’ll do most of my spending on this card. I’m a keeper just from the fee credit and earning multipliers.

    But what about the redemption of points?

    Recent findings suggest that well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners. It’s already a huge win.

    In a recent development, chase Travel’s ‘The Edit’ is a curated selection of nice hotels, which offer benefits similar to those provided by a travel agent or other luxury credit card booking platform. When booking a ‘The Edit’ property, you can expect breakfast for two, a $100 F&B credit, late check out and an upgrade subject to availability.

    Sources indicate that which leads me to the key bit! With the revamped Sapphire Reserve Card, there’s a new “Points Boost” feature, which offers up to two cents per point (25,000 points would cover $500, etc) for some flight or hotel purchases.

    This can be amazing value, with flights of $3,000 being grabbed for just 150,000 points, with no taxes and fees and the ability to still earn frequent flyer miles and elite status points, since the airline treats it like a cash ticket.

    According to recent reports, previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the new version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

    I am in Upcoming York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

    Typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

    According to recent reports, if I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

    BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive….

    Recent findings suggest that yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

    A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

    For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

    According to recent reports, if Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

    You can check out the upcoming 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.
